title: Comparing the Simulated Annealing and Robust Tabu Search Solvers
text: solve instances 30 100 facilities QAPLib. method gets 3 random restarts uses default settings.  Simulated annealing finishes much faster, solutions typically optimum. solution can modestly improved tuning (increasing) ft maxsteps. Robust tabu search spends time finds better solutions. cost per iteration grows number swap moves, quadratic n, default number iterations grows linearly n. run time therefore grows roughly cubically n. Larger QAPLIB instances tai256c (256 facilities) can added instances, single tabu search restart takes tens seconds, leave keep vignette fast build.
code: instances <- c("tai30a", "tai50a", "tai80a", "sko100a") reps <- 3  run <- function(p, method, ...) {   time <- system.time(a <- qap(p$A, p$B, method = method, ...))[["elapsed"]]   c(obj = unname(attr(a, "obj")), time = time) }  res <- do.call(rbind, lapply(instances, function(f) {   p <- read_qaplib(system.file("qaplib", paste0(f, ".dat"), package = "qap"))   sa <- run(p, "SA", rep = reps)   ro <- run(p, "RoTS", rep = reps)   data.frame(     instance = f,     n = nrow(p$A),     opt = p$opt,     SA_gap = (sa[["obj"]] - p$opt) / p$opt * 100,     RoTS_gap = (ro[["obj"]] - p$opt) / p$opt * 100,     SA_time = sa[["time"]],     RoTS_time = ro[["time"]]   ) })) knitr::kable(res, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,   col.names = c("Instance", "n", "Optimum", "SA gap (%)", "RoTS gap (%)",                 "SA time (s)", "RoTS time (s)")) op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1)) matplot(res$n, res[, c("SA_gap", "RoTS_gap")], type = "b", pch = 1:2,         lty = 1, col = 1:2, xlab = "n", ylab = "gap above optimum (%)",         main = "Solution quality") legend("topleft", legend = c("SA", "RoTS"), pch = 1:2, col = 1:2, lty = 1) matplot(res$n, res[, c("SA_time", "RoTS_time")], type = "b", pch = 1:2,         lty = 1, col = 1:2, log = "y", xlab = "n", ylab = "seconds",         main = "Run time") par(op)

title: Solve a Quadratic Assignment Problem — qap
text: problem assign \(n\) facilities \(n\) locations minimize total transportation interaction costs. Required flows facilities represented matrix \(\) distances locations given matrix \(B\). QAP seeks assignment minimizes sum flows times distance. assignment represented \(n \times n\) permutation matrix \(X\) used assign facilities locations order given permutation, objective can written $$\min_{X \\Pi}\; \mathrm{tr}(AXB^TX^T)$$ \(\Pi\) set valid \(n \times n\) permutation matrices. Note symmetric distances, distance matrix \(B\) need transposed. QAP originated facility location problem (Koopmans Beckmann, 1957) also applications data analysis (Hubert Schultz, 1976). NP-hard. Two heuristics available.

title: Solve a Quadratic Assignment Problem — qap
text: method = "SA" uses simulated annealing heuristic Burkard Rendl (1984), based Rendl's Fortran implementation QAPLIB. authors suggest can produce heuristic solutions problems 256 objects, although implementation enforce limit. Additional arguments method = "SA" : rep Positive integer number restarts. restarts can help local optima. Default: 1L. miter Positive integer number iterations fixed temperature. Increasing miter typically leads modest reduction optimality gap increasing runtime. Default: 2 * nrow(). fiter Factor least 1 miter grows cooling step. Larger values lead long runtimes. Default 1.1. ft Factor temperature decreases cooling step. increasing value, maxsteps also needs increased. Default 0.5 (strictly 0 1). maxsteps Positive integer maximum number cooling steps. search also stops earlier frozen, .e., objective value change whole step. default cooling rate typically happens problems less 150 objects default maxsteps 50 reached, however, larger problems can benefit increasing maxsteps. Default 50L. verbose Print parameter settings , restart, best current objective values, number cooling steps used, final temperature, run time; default FALSE. good starting point experiments set maxsteps large (e.g., 100000) slow cooling increasing ft 0.5 0.1 steps towards 1. Use verbose = TRUE see algorithm's behavior given parameters maxsteps stop simulated annealing early high final temperature.

title: Solve a Quadratic Assignment Problem — qap
text: method = "RoTS" uses robust tabu search Taillard (1991). repeatedly moves best pairwise exchange two facilities tabu, tabu tenure varies randomly around tenure iterations prevents facilities returning recently used locations. Moves accepted regardless tabu status give new best solution place facility location used aspiration iterations. Random numbers come R's generator, results can reproduced set.seed(). Additional arguments method = "RoTS" : rep Positive integer number restarts random permutations. restarts reduce dependence starting permutation. Default 1L. iter Positive integer number tabu search iterations per restart. run time grows linearly iter. Default 100 * nrow(). tenure Positive integer mean tabu tenure. actual tenure drawn uniformly 0.9 1.1 times value. longer tenure forbids moves pushes search away current region, shorter tenure makes greedy. Default nrow(). aspiration Nonnegative number iterations unused placement may override tabu status. Default 5 * nrow()^2. verbose Print parameter settings , restart, best current objective values, iteration best solution found (best_iter), number tabu moves taken aspiration (aspired), run time; default FALSE. Unlike simulated annealing, tabu search always runs iter iterations. tabu tenure controls strongly search pushed explore stays fixed run. defaults follow Taillard (1991) worked well many small QAPLIB problems small changes parameters tenure aspiration often make little difference. Use verbose = TRUE check best_iter: best solution found close iter, search still improving iter increased. found much earlier, rest run added little, smaller iter restarts may effective.
